Strait of Hormuz Status: October 6, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
6 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.15 + 0.87 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The Maritime Executive, Chosunbiz, and gCaptain report 12 seafarers were injured when a projectile struck an LR2 tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.

02 The closure picture remains contested: Iran says the strait will remain closed, while the Financial Times reports captains are being paid $100,000 a month to transit it.

03 Brent stood at $101.15, up 0.87% over 24 hours, as of 23:47 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the focal point of the crisis, with The Maritime Executive, Chosunbiz, and gCaptain all reporting that 12 seafarers were injured when a projectile struck an LR2 tanker in the strait. TheWire.in reports 11 of the injured crew members are Indian. The physical status of the waterway is contested: Iran says it will remain closed, while the Financial Times reports that captains are being paid $100,000 a month to transit it, indicating ships are still moving. Al Jazeera reports that ship attacks in the strait have surged, raising questions about whether elevated oil export volumes can be sustained. The product tanker Lipsi was hit on October 4 and is a continuing story, not a new development. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $101.15, up 0.87% over 24 hours, as of 23:47 UTC. The site's 59 indexed events in the last 24 hours reflect the pace of incident reporting across the waterway. As of 23:50 UTC, 203 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, easing over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.

Recorded
Brent down 3.1% in 24h
